player reports (ask 14: backend/api/player_reports.py and player_report_rules.py, mounted by main.py include_router): the five routes under /api/v1/player-reports and /api/v1/admin/player-reports, each route's reads named from this gate's own reached closure (every reached function's source and every reached string binding, scanned for SQL table words and ORM selects). The walk folds in every module that binds a shared name; no statement of a folded module is reached by these routes. The submit and the games read require a verified session (steam_sessions: main._session_seat and main._seat_attestation_verdict through main._strict_steam_session_ok) and the switch (runtime_settings, key player_reports_accept, player_reports.SWITCH_SQL), and read the caller's finished games of 14 days through one statement (player_reports.GAMES_SQL, whose CTE names are g_1v1, g_2v2, g_1v2, g_ffa and listed) over matches, team_matches, ovt_matches, ffa_matches and ffa_match_players, each by an explicit column list: from matches it selects id, ended_at, player1_id and player2_id, and reads invalidated_at and photon_room_id in the WHERE clause alone; from team_matches id, ended_at and the four player ids; from ovt_matches id, ended_at and the three player ids; from ffa_matches id and ended_at, with ffa_match_players' match_id, player_id and absent; each game table's invalidated_at in the WHERE clause alone; it joins players for id, steam_id and display_name and reads deleted_at in the WHERE clause. The games read, a GET, reaches through the verified-reads route class every GET carries (read_gate.ReadGateRoute: the mode from runtime_settings, the session from steam_sessions, the operator key from api_operator_keys), also reads players (the caller's id by steam id, PLAYER_SQL) and player_reports (the caller's own reports in the window and the caller's count of 24 hours, MY_REPORTS_SQL and RECENT_SQL), and answers a projection: per game its kind, id and end time, per other player the steam id, the display name and whether the caller has reported them, and the count of reports the caller has left. The submit reads players (the two accounts' ids, PLAYER_SQL) and player_reports (the same report and the caller's count of 24 hours, DUPLICATE_SQL and RECENT_SQL), takes the two accounts' advisory locks (main._identity_lock_many, where the scan's words and and in come from a comment's FOR UPDATE and UPDATE in and name no table), writes player_reports (one row, INSERT_SQL) and player_report_logs (the attached log: the tail of the text after the credential rule, gzip; INSERT_LOG_SQL) and deletes the player_report_logs rows past their retention day (RETENTION_SQL); it answers a fixed body (ok, log_stored) or a refusal code. The three admin routes read admin_users (main._is_admin, an ORM select of AdminUser) and verify the admin signature over their own action word and target (main._verify_admin_hmac). The list, a GET through the same route class, reads player_reports joined to players (both accounts' steam ids and display names, the closer's display name) with the existence of a player_report_logs row (player_reports._LIST_HEAD and COUNTS_SQL), and answers seventeen named fields per report and two counts. The log view, a GET through the same route class, reads one player_reports row's dates and its player_report_logs gz (LOG_META_SQL, LOG_GZ_SQL) and answers the text through main._scrub_bug_log, which reads deleted_steam_ids (main._purged_steam_ids). The close reads players (the closer's id, PLAYER_SQL), updates one open player_reports row (CLOSE_SQL, STATUS_SQL) and runs the same retention delete, answering a fixed body. No handler reads a Match ORM row or a whole row of a game table, and the games answer carries a game's kind, id and end time only, so no W1 private Match column can reach an output. Static classification: handler-implementation drift (another matches column, or a whole-row answer) would need re-review.
